schema_notes: expected_tool_call is true when query_research_corpus should be called for this question, false when it should not.
trap_class groups questions by what kind of misroute they're designed to surface; it is not sent to the model, only used for the per-trap-class accuracy breakdown in eval_tool_selection.py.

off_corpus_biomed convention: an in-domain biomedical question the ai-research-assistant corpus may not actually cover is still expected_tool_call=true. The tool description promises to report contextSufficient=false for coverage gaps; the client cannot know corpus contents in advance and should still call the tool based on topical intent, mirroring the off_corpus_biomed convention in ai-agent-module's classification_set.json.

biomed_general_knowledge: clinically-flavored questions answerable as common knowledge, not requiring a peer-reviewed source lookup. expected_tool_call=false, though this is the most genuinely debatable trap class in the set — a stricter reading of 'biomedical' could argue the other way. Worth watching in the per-trap-class breakdown.
calculation_in_biomed_clothing / arithmetic dressed in medical vocabulary: expected_tool_call=false, since these are pure arithmetic that the corpus tool cannot perform.

document_shaped_non_biomed: questions phrased to want a sourced/document-grounded answer, but in a domain the tool description explicitly excludes (legal, physics, humanities). expected_tool_call=false.
